items.title: Neal Caine interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, September 26, 2019
items.q: I played with Diana Krall and I played with Harry Connick

ctx.x: Was there a distinction playing behind a vocalist, like Betty Carter? Did she require something different than Elvin Jones did?

In general, yeah. Vocalists do. I mean it’s funny, Betty Carter was such a unique vocalist, I always conceptualized her as a sax player kind of, in a way. When I thought about her like that it made more sense to me. She was great, man. She was so challenging. Because she had a lot of different forms and speeds and a lot of it was kind of cues to the next section and they’d be different every night. So in that respect it wasn’t the usual just play a standard kind of singer. But yeah, I mean I played with Diana…
Do you have a thought method that kicks in if you have to play “There Will Never Be Another You” in A flat instead of E flat?
